      "post_date": "2026-10-25T04:08:00.710Z",
      "raw_markdown": "I've ported my solution to Kaggle (accelerator: RTX PRO 6000) and am testing it before the deadline. Performance varies a lot between instances, which I'd expect to be standardized:\n\n* **Startup time:** my inference server takes anywhere from 10 to 60 minutes to start, with the same notebook and inputs.\n* **Throughput:** the instances that start slowly also run about 10% slower afterwards. I suspect CPU contention or different host hardware, but I can't tell from inside the session.\n\nQuestions:\n\n1. Is this variation known? Is the hardware behind RTX PRO 6000 sessions meant to be identical?\n2. Does the same setup (input mounting, startup) run before a submission's rerun, and does it count toward the 9-hour runtime limit?\n3. Can we do anything on our side to get a consistent instance?\n\n**Earlier issues (now resolved):**\n\n* The draft session got stuck at \"adding data\" whenever any input was attached, even a 1 KB test dataset (it showed \"Downloaded 1/1 files: 1.12KiB [100%]\"). With no inputs attached, it started immediately. It turned out to be progressing very slowly rather than stuck, and mounting now works.\n* For a while, turning on the notebook failed with \"Oops something went wrong. An unknown error occurred.\"\n\nHas anyone else seen this?",
